open.fact: FPL Report 2171 was not opened by 065 and was not opened in this review. No face gauge, core, density, cell, bond, stress or specimen count was checked. The not-admissible judgment stands because the source is absent. Opening it would still leave the product-form limit unless the coupons are this beryllium sandwich.
This review did not repeat the search for a titanium metal-face honeycomb wrinkling table. 065's statement that none was found is unchecked.
The beryllium report's Table IX did not yield a specimen count under the OCR used here. 065's statement that the count was not recovered is consistent with that. The count stays unknown.

FPL 1810-A reports E_L along the flutes as 16,700 psi for core A, averaged from 13,800 and 19,600. That is the direction normal to the facings. E_R 0.99 psi and E_T 4.53 psi are the head-to-head readings and are not that modulus. Neither 065 nor this review reduced a classical Q from E_L. The coupons are spring steel on resin paper, so a computed Q would still not transfer.

Membrane stress pR/(4 tf), using pressures from this seat's 064 run, lies 1.4 to 4.7 percent under BETA*0.33*sqrt(E*Ec*tf/tc). The gap grows with core thickness over face thickness, which is the shape of the cure term. The thermal field was not recomputed, so that residual is not closed. It does not close the factor BETA.

Section 6.5.1 of NTRS 19730016169 does not restate the braze alloy on the edgewise coupons. Section 9.3 says alloy code 7, Ag-27Cu-10Sn, was used for scale-up testing. The card's identification is supported at program level and is not reprinted on the coupon paragraph.
